# DuplexJev-4B-Para (v1.4)

📄 Paper: [arXiv:2610.02638](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02638) · Code: [github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev](https://github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev) · Release note: [hearing the whole clip](https://github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev/blob/main/research/2026-11-full-length.md)

**The small DuplexJev, now with live turn-taking on par with the 32B model: it knows when the user has finished.**

> **v1.4 (2026-11-04)** replaces v1.3 (2026-10-22). Earlier versions stay available as revisions `v1.3`, `v1.2`, `v1.1`
> and `v1.0` (`--revision v1.3` in vLLM, `revision="v1.3"` in `from_pretrained`).
>
> **Needs `duplexjev-vllm>=0.4` (or `duplexjev>=0.7`).** v1.4 hears the whole audio clip (the Qwen3-ASR encoder emits 6.5
> audio tokens per second, not 6.25); the checkpoint sets `"audio_full_length": true` in `config.json` and the new
> plugin reads it. Older checkpoints keep their old behaviour.

Architecture: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B encoder + connector + Qwen3-4B, 4.2 B parameters, bf16, ~10 GB GPU memory.

## What changed

- **Retrained in one pass** from v1.1 on the complete data mix (everything v1.2 and v1.3 added, Japanese included), on the
  true audio length, instead of stacking one more stage on v1.3. Adds the emotion corpora and transcription fixes from
  DuplexJev-32B-Para v1.4 / v1.5.
- **Turn-taking stage**: the live end-of-turn data behind DuplexJev-4B-Para-LiveTurn (the assistant's previous message
  as context, decisions right after a short pause, natural two-speaker English, background speech and noise) plus
  accent data, with the full mix replayed (a rank-64 LoRA on the LLM, merged here; the connector keeps training).

## Results (v1.3 → v1.4, same evaluation code and items; each model with its own audio-length setting)

**End of turn**

| | v1.3 | **v1.4** |
|---|---:|---:|
| Smart Turn v3.2 test set, accuracy (P(finished) ≥ 0.5, n = 8,749) | 71.0 | **92.9** |
| Smart Turn v3.2 test set, AUC | 0.811 | **0.977** |
| LiveKit eot-bench, English false cut-offs at a 300 ms budget | 25.8 % | **21.8 %** |
| LiveKit eot-bench, Chinese false cut-offs at a 300 ms budget | 42.9 % | **39.6 %** |
| LiveKit eot-bench, English false cut-offs at 600 ms | 13.0 % | **11.6 %** |

eot-bench numbers use audio plus the assistant's previous message, as the Pipecat / LiveKit plugins send it (our fast
setting). Smart Turn v3.2 on the same English data: 35.2 % at 300 ms.

**Emotion**

| | v1.3 | **v1.4** |
|---|---:|---:|
| LISTEN, emotion from voice (LISTEN-EM) | 25.6 | **30.9** |
| LISTEN, neutral text (LISTEN-NT) | 44.5 | **49.9** |
| ESD Chinese / English (held-out speakers) | 90.8 / 81.0 | **95.0 / 83.5** |
| CREMA-D | 81.0 | **84.0** |

**Stress and pauses**

| | v1.3 | **v1.4** |
|---|---:|---:|
| StressPresso | 80.7 | **87.6** |
| StressTest | 80.3 | **81.7** |
| DEBATE: which word is stressed / does the pause change the meaning | 87.7 / 79.5 | **91.8 / 84.1** |
| Stressed word, Chinese / English (unseen sentences) | 85.1 / 87.2 | **88.0 / 89.8** |

**Non-verbal sounds and speaking style**

| | v1.3 | **v1.4** |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cough (VocalSound / NonverbalTTS) | 89.4 / 83.4 | **94.5 / 91.4** |
| Sigh (VocalSound / NonverbalSpeech-38K) | 90.5 / 90.2 | **93.9 / 93.3** |
| Laughter in Chinese conversation (MagicData, held-out) | 75.0 | **91.7** |
| Speaking style (EARS / Expresso) | 68.2 / 94.7 | **72.3 / 98.3** |

## Serve with vLLM

```bash
pip install "vllm[audio]>=0.29" "duplexjev-vllm>=0.4"
vllm serve adventists-ai/DuplexJev-4B-Para --max-model-len 4096
# previous version: add --revision v1.3
```

Decision prompts are the same as for [DuplexJev-4B-Turn](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/DuplexJev-4B-Turn); see [`examples/vllm_client.py`](https://github.com/adventists-ai/duplexjev/blob/main/examples/vllm_client.py). Always offer a "none" option for stress and non-verbal questions. For
live end of turn in a voice agent, use `pipecat-duplexjev` or `livekit-plugins-duplexjev`, which also send the
assistant's previous message. For conversation, send the user audio as the user turn (`<|audio|>`) with ordinary chat
history and sample as usual.

## Limitations

- For transcription in Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai and Arabic the 32B model
  ([DuplexJev-32B-Para](https://huggingface.co/adventists-ai/DuplexJev-32B-Para)) is much stronger.
- Asked about itself, it may describe abilities (seeing images, speaking) that this checkpoint does not have on its own:
  it takes speech and text and replies in text.
- Speaker judgments are coarse and must not be used to identify or verify people; emotion outputs must not be used to
  make decisions about individuals.

- Non-commercial data:
  - Stress: DEBATE (github.com/SmileHnu/DEBATE), Stress-17K and TinyStress-15K (slprl);
  - Expresso (Meta), EARS (Meta) and NonVerbalSpeech-38K, all CC BY-NC 4.0;
  - ESD (research only); SmoothConv (CC BY-NC);
  - Conversation replay: user turns from wilzzzz/paralinguistic_dialogues (no licence stated on the dataset card; used for non-commercial research), SmoothConv (CC BY-NC), AISHELL-1 (Apache-2.0), LibriSpeech (CC BY 4.0); target replies generated by Qwen3-4B (Apache-2.0); spoken chat questions synthesised with CosyVoice2 (Apache-2.0).
- Added in v1.2 (non-commercial or share-alike): Emilia JA/KO (CC BY-NC 4.0); VIVOS (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); a licensed Mandarin
  conversational corpus with paralinguistic annotation (MagicData, purchased licence; audio not redistributed).
- Added in v1.2 (other): Emilia-YODAS JA/KO (CC BY 4.0), YODAS2 (CC BY 3.0), Zeroth-Korean (CC BY 4.0), FLEURS train split
  (CC BY 4.0; the test split was never used), Common Voice 17 ar/ru (CC0). Labels were re-checked, and for unlabelled
  YODAS2 clips produced, with Qwen3-ASR-0.6B (Apache-2.0); continuation targets were written by Qwen3-32B (Apache-2.0).
- Added in v1.3: Japanese speech from Emilia JA (CC BY-NC 4.0), Emilia-YODAS JA (CC BY 4.0), Common Voice ja (CC0) and other
  Japanese speech data, used for non-commercial research; every label re-checked with Qwen3-ASR-0.6B (Apache-2.0),
  continuation targets written by Qwen3-32B (Apache-2.0). The held-out Emilia JA shard used for testing was never trained on.
- Added in v1.4 (non-commercial or share-alike): EmotionTalk (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); DailyTalk (CC BY-SA 4.0); accents from

- Added in v1.4 (other): CSEMOTIONS (Apache-2.0), EMNS (Apache-2.0), JL-Corpus (CC0), Emozionalmente (CC BY 4.0), SUBESCO
  (CC BY 4.0); FLEURS dev split (CC BY 4.0; the test split was never used); accents from VCTK (CC BY 4.0) and

- Other data:
  - VocalSound (CC BY-SA 4.0), NonverbalTTS (audio from VoxCeleb and Expresso);
  - VoxCeleb1 (CC BY 4.0), AISHELL-1 (Apache-2.0), LibriSpeech (CC BY 4.0);
  - ARC (CC BY-SA 4.0), OpenBookQA, CommonsenseQA (MIT).
- Base models keep their licences: Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-ASR-0.6B are Apache-2.0 (Alibaba Cloud); the Qwen3-4B licence
  is included. The LLM weights are Qwen3-4B with LoRAs merged in.

# Pocket TTS ONNX

ONNX export of [Pocket TTS](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/pocket-tts) for lightweight multilingual text-to-speech with zero-shot voice cloning.

## Model Description

Pocket TTS is a compact text-to-speech model from Kyutai that supports voice cloning from short audio samples. This ONNX export provides:

- **Zero-shot voice cloning** from any audio reference
- **Multilingual bundles** for `english_2026-04`, `french_24l`, `german`, `german_24l`, `italian`, `italian_24l`, `portuguese`, `portuguese_24l`, `spanish`, and `spanish_24l`
- **INT8 quantized models** for fast CPU inference
- **Streaming support** with adaptive chunking for real-time playback
- **Temperature control** for generation diversity
- **Dual model architecture** for flexible flow matching

## Architecture

This export uses a **dual model split** for the Flow LM:

```
flow_lm_main   - Transformer/conditioner (produces conditioning vectors)
flow_lm_flow   - Flow network only (Euler integration for latent sampling)
```

This architecture enables:
- **Temperature control**: Adjust generation diversity via noise scaling
- **Variable LSD steps**: Trade off speed vs quality
- **External flow loop**: Full control over the sampling process

## Performance

Performance depends on the selected language bundle, precision, CPU, and `lsd_steps`.

- 6-layer bundles such as `english_2026-04`, `german`, `italian`, `portuguese`, and `spanish` are much smaller and faster than the `*_24l` bundles.
- INT8 bundles substantially reduce `flow_lm_main`, `flow_lm_flow`, and `mimi_decoder` size for CPU inference.
- `mimi_encoder.onnx` and `text_conditioner.onnx` remain FP32.

### Optimized Inference

Thread count is automatically tuned to avoid over-subscription on the small sequential matmuls in the autoregressive loop (`intra_op_num_threads=min(cpu_count, 4)`, `inter_op_num_threads=1`). This alone provides a **~2x speedup** over default ORT settings on multi-core machines.

### Decoding Strategy

- **Offline (`generate`)**: Uses **threaded parallel decoding** — the mimi decoder runs in a background thread, decoding 12-frame chunks while the flow loop generates the next frames. This overlaps generation and decoding for maximum throughput.
- **Streaming (`stream`)**: Uses **adaptive chunking** (starts at 2 frames). This ensures instant start (low TTFB) while scaling up chunk sizes for throughput.

## Usage

```python
from pocket_tts_onnx import PocketTTSOnnx

# Load the English bundle (INT8 by default)
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(
    models_dir="onnx",
    language="english_2026-04",
)

# Generate speech with built-in voice state
audio = tts.generate(
    text="Hello, this is a test.",
    voice="alba",
)

# Generate speech with voice cloning from audio
audio = tts.generate(
    text="Hello, this is a test of voice cloning.",
    voice="reference_sample.wav"
)

# Save output
tts.save_audio(audio, "output.wav")
```

### Temperature Control

Adjust generation diversity with the `temperature` parameter:

```python
# More deterministic (lower temperature)
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(temperature=0.3)

# Default balance
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(temperature=0.7)

# More diverse/expressive (higher temperature)
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(temperature=1.0)
```

### LSD Steps

Trade off speed vs quality with `lsd_steps`:

```python
# Default
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(lsd_steps=1)

# Slower, potentially smoother
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(lsd_steps=4)
```

### Streaming Mode

For real-time applications with low time-to-first-audio:

```python
for chunk in tts.stream("Hello world!", voice="reference_sample.wav"):
    play_audio(chunk)  # Process each chunk as it arrives
```

### Language Bundles

```python
# German bundle with built-in voice
tts = PocketTTSOnnx(language="german", precision="fp32")
audio = tts.generate("Hallo zusammen. Dies ist ein deutscher Test.", voice="alba")
```

Built-in voice names are loaded from each bundle's metadata. Voice cloning also accepts:

- a reference audio path
- a `.safetensors` prompt-state file
- a precomputed embedding array

### Legacy Layout

Root-level files under `onnx/` and the root `tokenizer.model` are still present for backward compatibility with older integrations that expect the original single-model layout.

New integrations should use the per-language bundle directories under `onnx/<language>/`.

### Command Line

```bash
python generate.py "Hello, this is a test." alba output.wav --language english_2026-04
python generate.py "Hallo zusammen." samples/reference.wav output.wav --language german --precision fp32
```

## Requirements


- Built-in voice states are fetched from `kyutai/pocket-tts` via Hugging Face.
- Voice cloning from audio uses the exported `mimi_encoder.onnx`.

# MireskaVoice (Ming-3.0-tts 版)

邪影芳灵（Mireska Sunbreeze / Dark Willow，Dota 2 英雄）中文音色的 **Ming-3.0-tts-0.5B 微调模型**。

基于 inclusionAI 开源的 [Ming-3.0-tts-0.5B](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-0.5b)（BailingMM 底座，bf16 约 2.8GB），使用 899 条游戏内中文配音（879 训练 + 20 留出）进行 LoRA 微调（r=8/alpha=16 + 全量训练 audio/flow/stop/spk heads，可训练参数 206M）。说话人条件为 campplus 嵌入：训练用目标片段自身嵌入（speaker_dropout 0.5），推理用同角色参考片段嵌入（仓库内附带 `eval/ref_real_dw_0857.wav`）。

> 姊妹仓库：[wjcwqc/MireskaVoice](https://huggingface.co/wjcwqc/MireskaVoice)（OmniVoice 微调版，音色相似度更高，见下方对比）。

## 目录结构

| 路径 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `merged/` | LoRA 已合并的独立模型（`sft.export` 导出，标准 HF 目录，直接加载即用） |
| `lora/step_00000906.pt` | 原始训练 checkpoint（LoRA + heads，2.4GB，可用 `python -m sft.export` 重新导出或 `--resume` 续训） |
| `training/` | 训练配置（yaml + resolved config）、数据准备/推理脚本、完整训练日志 |
| `eval/` | 20 条留出文本评估报告 JSON + 6 条生成样本 + 真人参考片段 + 说话人嵌入 |

## 使用方法

需要 Ming-3.0-tts 官方仓库代码（`pip install -r requirements.txt`）：

```bash
# 1. 克隆推理代码
git clone https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts   # 仓库根需含 ming_tts.py 等

# 2. 下载本仓库
huggingface-cli download wjcwqc/MireskaVoice-ming --local-dir ./MireskaVoice-ming

# 3. 批量合成（自带脚本，campplus 参考嵌入自动从 ref_real_dw_0857.wav 提取）
python ./MireskaVoice-ming/training/infer_ming.py \
    --model_path ./MireskaVoice-ming/merged \
    --texts texts.json \
    --out_dir out \
    --spk_wav ./MireskaVoice-ming/eval/ref_real_dw_0857.wav \
    --device cuda:0
```

`texts.json` 格式：`{"tid1": "文本1", "tid2": "文本2"}`。

单句推理（官方接口）：

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "<Ming-3.0-tts 仓库>")
from ming_tts import MingTTS
model = MingTTS("./MireskaVoice-ming/merged", device="cuda:0", text_normalization=False)
```

推理参数（评估所用）：seed=1895，cfg=2.0，temperature=0.0。硬件参考：单卡 4GB 显存即可（bf16 + gradient checkpointing 训练实测通过）。

## 效果评估（20 条留出文本，真人片段互相相似度基线 0.6994）

| 模型 | CER（字错率）↓ | spk-sim（音色相似度）↑ |
|---|---|---|
| **Ming-3.0-tts LoRA（本模型）** | **0.0416** | 0.6454 |
| OmniVoice 微调（姊妹仓库） | 0.028 | 0.758 |
| CosyVoice3 零样本 | 0.056 | 0.706 |
| VITS 微调 | 0.306 | 0.572 |

16/20 句零字错；错误集中在专有名词（铁雾城→鐵屋城、米瑞斯嘉→米瑞斯加）。逐句明细见 `eval/eval_report.json`，完整报告见 `REPORT.md`。

## 训练信息

- **数据**：899 条（879 训练 + 20 留出），32kHz 原始音频；数据准备脚本 `training/prep_ming_data.py`（campplus 嵌入随样本缓存）
- **方法**：LoRA r=8 alpha=16 dropout=0.05，目标层 q/k/v/o_proj；全量训练 linear_proj_audio、flowloss、stop_head、spk_head
- **超参**：lr 1e-5 → 1e-6（warmup 100 步），10 epochs = 906 步，max_tokens_per_batch 1024，bf16，gradient checkpointing，speaker_dropout 0.5
- **硬件**：单卡 RTX 3050 Ti Laptop 4GB，约 2 小时 40 分；loss 0.566 → ~0.50
- **过程**：配置 `training/lora_config.yaml`、完整日志 `training/train_full.log`（逐步 JSON 见 `training/train_log.jsonl`）

# DAC (Descript Audio Codec) 16 kHz — LiteRT (CompiledModel GPU)

[Descript Audio Codec](https://github.com/descriptinc/descript-audio-codec) running **on-device on
the LiteRT CompiledModel GPU** (ML Drift). The convolutional encoder/decoder run on the GPU; the RVQ
runs on CPU. **43:1 compression** (1 s → 12×50 codes), **RTF ≈ 0.82** (faster than real-time) on Pixel 8a.

## Files
- `dac_16khz_encoder_fp16.tflite` (43 MB) — `audio[1,1,16000]` → `latent[1,1024,50]`, GPU.
- `dac_16khz_deconly_zs_fp16.tflite` (105 MB) — `latent[1,1024,50]` → `audio`, GPU.
- `dac_rvq.bin` (1.2 MB) — RVQ weights (12 codebooks) for the CPU quantizer (float32 LE).

## Pipeline
```
audio -> encoder.tflite (GPU) -> z -> RVQ.encode (CPU) -> codes[12,50]
      -> RVQ.decode (CPU) -> z_q -> decoder.tflite (GPU) -> audio
```

## On-device (Pixel 8a, Tensor G3 — verified)
encoder **367/367** + decoder **398/398** nodes on the LiteRT GPU delegate (`LITERT_CL`, 1 partition,
no CPU fallback); warm RTF ~0.82; reconstruction **corr 1.0** vs PyTorch DAC.

## Why the split
The decoder's `ConvTranspose1d` are rewritten to a GPU-clean **zero-stuff** form (the real DAC's
odd stride-5 transposed conv fails converter legalization, and `TRANSPOSE_CONV` is rejected by Mali).
The RVQ uses `EMBEDDING_LOOKUP` + int64 indices (Mali-rejected) so it runs on CPU. So the float conv
graph stays fully on the GPU.

Android sample + conversion/validation scripts:
**https://github.com/john-rocky/LiteRT-Models/tree/main/dac**
